summary: round 2, delta since abb31768ff8b7874080512953fb66a86fa372520: F-1, F-2, F-3, F-4 fixed (all round-1 majors); F-5 to F-21, F-23 and F-25 also fixed. No blocker or major remains, so pass. Follow-ups: 1 new minor (F-26: the N-2 throwing response fires only if the SPA reads the 2xx body) and 3 infos (F-22 and F-24 carried, trimmed to what remains; new F-27).

findings.message: Firefox never ran in the red runs (round 2 red evidence: Firefox not installed), so the firefox project of the main configuration is unproven until the stack exists. In jsdom the dialog is a shim, so focus containment is proven only by the e2e keyboard spec. The date-fill, typecheck and lint parts of round 1 are done.
findings.suggestion: Install the Firefox browser for Playwright and run the main configuration on both projects once the stack exists.

findings.message: The TypeScript 7 to 6 downgrade still has no stated reason. tests/README.md now records the extra test-only dev dependencies and defers the TypeScript line to the react-engineer.
findings.suggestion: State why TypeScript 6 is used, or have the react-engineer record it with the ADR-0001 version pins.

findings.message: throwingResponse is a 2xx Response with no body and no Content-Type whose json/text readers reject. The three N-2 tests (toggle, create, save) see the unexpected error only if the SPA reads the success body of setTodoDone, createTodo and updateTodo. A compliant client that skips parsing when there is no JSON Content-Type (for example to handle 204 from logout and delete), or a screen that re-queries or navigates without reading those bodies, never meets the throw, so these tests would fail against a correct build and N10 may not weaken them (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
findings.suggestion: Give the throwing Response a Content-Type: application/json header, and state in web/tests/README.md that src/api/client.ts reads the JSON body of every 2xx response that has one, so N10 builds to that seam.

findings.message: The e2e script chains the three runs with POSIX shell syntax ($?, test -a). pnpm runs scripts with cmd on Windows, where it fails. The sdd section 11 prerequisites name no operating system.
findings.suggestion: If Windows matters, chain the runs with a small Node script (or npm-run-all) that runs all three and fails if any failed.
